title: SriLankan links to 17 Maldives destinations - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 28 (Daily Mirror) - SriLankan Airlines has expanded its regional network by signing a new interline agreement with Island Aviation Services, operating as Maldivian (Q2), enabling passengers to travel seamlessly to 17 domestic destinations across the Maldives under a single ticket.

The agreement allows passengers to book combined itineraries on SriLankan Airlines and Maldivian using a single electronic ticket for both inbound and outbound travel via Velana International Airport in Malé and Gan International Airport on Gan Island.

The partnership links SriLankan Airlines' international network with Maldivian's domestic services, offering easier access to remote and popular islands in the Maldives. The airline said the move is expected to benefit both leisure and business travellers by providing smoother transfers throughout the archipelago.

SriLankan Airlines currently operates three daily flights to Velana International Airport in Malé and two weekly flights to Gan International Airport, providing strong connectivity between Sri Lanka and the Maldives while offering onward connections through its international network.

The airline said the interline agreement would also create new opportunities for travel agents, tour operators, corporate travel planners and individual travellers by simplifying bookings and supporting passenger growth on the Malé and Gan routes.

"Our collaboration with Maldivian represents an important milestone in expanding our regional footprint and enhancing travel convenience for our customers. By integrating our global network with Maldivian's domestic connectivity, we are unlocking greater access across the Maldives while creating new opportunities for growth across key commercial segments," Head of Commercial Dimuthu Tennakoon said.

Maldives Manager Nayomi Tennakoon said the partnership provides passengers with seamless access from SriLankan Airlines' global network through Malé and Gan to numerous domestic destinations across the Maldives on a single itinerary.

SriLankan Airlines said the initiative reflects its continued commitment to improving connectivity, convenience and travel options across the region.

The national carrier serves 130 destinations in 63 countries, including codeshare services, and operates direct flights to 33 destinations with an all-Airbus fleet comprising A330-200/300 and A320/321 aircraft.

title: Ganja-laced meals at roadside eateries cost consumers dearly - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Shane Seneviratne

Colombo, July 28 (Daily Mirror) - Judicial Medical Officer (JMO) at the Peradeniya Teaching Hospital, Dr Palitha Bandara Subasinghe, raised concerns over reports that some wayside eateries are using ganja (cannabis) leaves in meat dishes to enhance flavour, a practice that is illegal and could have serious consequences for motorists.

According to Dr. Subasinghe, drivers who unknowingly consume such food may test positive for cannabis if they are subjected to a medical examination following a traffic-related offence, leaving them vulnerable to legal action despite never intentionally using an intoxicant.

"There have been instances where drivers, who firmly maintain they have never consumed narcotic substances, were found to have cannabis compounds in their urine during medical examinations," he said.

He explained that many long-distance and commercial drivers rely on roadside eateries for their daily meals, making them particularly vulnerable if banned substances are secretly added to food.

Dr. Subasinghe warned that the issue raises a serious legal and public health concern, as innocent motorists could be prosecuted for driving under the influence after unknowingly consuming food prepared with cannabis.

He called on Public Health Inspectors (PHIs) and other relevant authorities to conduct regular inspections and take strict legal action against food establishments found using ganja in cooking.

"Using cannabis in food preparation is not only unlawful but also places unsuspecting consumers at risk of serious legal consequences," he stressed.

title: Hospital capacity crisis adds to dengue death toll: Specialist warns - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Chaturanga Pradeep Samarawickrama

Colombo, July 28 (Daily Mirror) - It is regrettable that some patients who require medical treatment and special attention as inpatients are returning home without being admitted to hospitals due to the current overcrowding, which has become a contributing factor in the increase in dengue-related deaths, Specialist Dr Chamal Sanjeewa said.

He said hospitals are under severe pressure due to the rising number of dengue patients, with both government and private hospitals exceeding their capacity to admit patients.

Dr Sanjeewa said the main causes behind dengue-related deaths were the worsening of the disease and complications arising from it. He said nearly 60 dengue-related deaths have been reported so far, with four key factors contributing to these fatalities.

According to him, the first factor is patients delaying medical treatment until the disease reaches a critical stage.

The second is the inability of some patients who require inpatient care to receive admission due to overcrowding in hospitals. He said some patients who need close monitoring and special medical attention are being sent home due to limited hospital capacity.

The third factor is possible shortcomings in the treatment provided to hospitalised patients. However, Dr Sanjeewa said there were no officially confirmed complaints or evidence that dengue deaths had occurred due to medical negligence.

The fourth factor is patients succumbing to complications and the severity of the disease while receiving treatment in hospitals.

He said that among these factors, most dengue-related deaths during the current outbreak have occurred due to patients seeking treatment after the disease had worsened and due to complications caused by the illness.

Dr Sanjeewa added that improved public awareness about dengue symptoms has helped reduce deaths caused by delays in seeking treatment. He said people, including children and adults, are now more likely to seek advice from specialist doctors or family physicians at the early stages of illness.

title: US$2.5Mn cyber heist; COPF covers up the top brass: UNP - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 28 (Daily Mirror) - The United National Party (UNP) yesterday charged that the Committee on Public Finance (COPF) had failed to identify the shortcomings of senior officials in connection with the cybercrime, while highlighting that the US$2.5 million heist had occurred due to the failure of the Finance Minister and the Secretary to the Finance Ministry to monitor the transition of powers from the Central Bank to the Public Debt Management Office.

The UNP said in a statement that the COPF report discusses the hacking and the theft, but has defended the higher officials and the top brass whose shortcomings led to the theft.

"The report uses terms such as 'systematic failure' and 'procedural gaps' but has been careful not to mention anyone who could be held accountable. The easiest way to escape accountability in today's politics is to blame the system for any shortcoming rather than identify those who are responsible.

"The Treasury Secretary is responsible for public funds, while the Finance Minister must take responsibility on behalf of the political leadership of the government." The report clearly states that there were shortcomings in the internal handling of the transition, the provision of guidelines and the administration. However, no allegations have been made against any senior official. Instead, only lower-ranking officers have been blamed. Accordingly, four officials have already been interdicted for neglect of duty. The report refers only to issues relating to language and coordination. This amounts to double standards. Higher officials who designed the systems appear to have defended themselves. Negligence relating to IT systems actually invited cyber thieves to act.

"The government has attempted to portray the theft as a sophisticated cybercrime. This is not the truth.

"The External Resources Department used an outdated email service that became operational in 2016 but had been out of service since 2025. Hackers began their activities in mid-November last year. Prior warnings issued by KPMG and the Sri Lanka National Centre for Cyber Security (SLCERT) were ignored. This indicates a failure on the part of the leadership.

"There was an 18-month period to transfer debt management powers from the Central Bank to the Public Debt Management Office. The Public Debt Management Office was established in December 2024. A coordination committee was required to be set up for the transition under Section 8 of the Public Debt Management Act. This committee was responsible for implementing work assigned by the Finance Minister. However, the minister failed to appoint the relevant persons in terms of Section 7 of the Act. The Central Bank signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Public Debt Management Office in January 2026, while the theft had already taken place between November 2025 and January 2026. Therefore, the government has concealed the truth from the public.

"The Treasury Secretary refused to appear before COPF from December 2025 to January 2026. COPF stated in its report that it had no mandate to engage in legal proceedings relating to the theft. However, the power over public finance is vested in Parliament under Article 148 of the Constitution. COPF avoided naming the Finance Minister and the Secretary to the Finance Ministry as those responsible."

title: Businessman arrested in Gampola over Rs. 2 Mn bribery scheme for hospital tender - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 28 (Daily Mirror) - Officers from the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) have arrested a businessman and another individual in Gampola for allegedly soliciting, accepting, and aiding in a bribe of Rs. 2,000,000.

The case stems from the bidding process to supply food ingredients for the Peradeniya Teaching Hospital's kitchen for the year 2027. According to investigators, the suspect had obtained official tender application forms under the names of his father and uncle. He offered to withhold these competing bids so that the complainant could secure the supply contract.

During negotiations, the main suspect initially demanded a bribe of Rs. 3 million, which was later reduced to Rs. 2.5 million, before eventually settling on Rs. 2 million.

Following a raid on July 27, 2026, CIABOC investigation officers arrested the suspects at Ratgala, near the Gampola Post Office. The businessman, identified as Arunagiri Nadar Logendran, was taken into custody at around 9:13 PM, while his accomplice, Logendran Sivaraj, was arrested shortly after at around 9:43 PM.

Both suspects face charges of soliciting, receiving, and aiding and abetting a bribe, and are scheduled to be produced before the Gampola Magistrate's Court for further legal proceedings.

title: India recall Jadeja for Sri Lanka Tests - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
July.28 (Mirror Sports) - Shubman Gill will lead India in a two-Test series against Sri Lanka, with the opening match set to begin in Galle on August 15 as part of the ICC World Test Championship 2025-27.

The biggest talking point is the return of all-rounder Ravindra Jadeja, who is back in India's Test squad for the first time since January after recovering from a tennis elbow injury that kept him sidelined since May.

Sai Sudharsan and Jasprit Bumrah have also been named in the squad, although both remain subject to fitness.

KL Rahul has been appointed vice-captain, while Rishabh Pant, Yashasvi Jaiswal and Dhruv Jurel bolster the batting line-up. Kuldeep Yadav will partner Jadeja in the spin department, while Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna and Gurnoor Brar provide the pace options.

India head into the series looking to bounce back after recent Test series defeats to New Zealand, South Africa and Australia. However, they have won their last two Test series in Sri Lanka, claiming victories in 2015 and 2017.

The first Test will be played in Galle from August 15-19, with the second scheduled for Colombo from August 23-27.
